then.text: Come back any time. The pools are free. The towels are not.
Back again, are you? The pools have been quiet and my Brook creatures have been practising. Mostly sulking, but it counts. Fancy a rematch?

else.text: Once a day, love. Even water needs a rest before it takes on another mountain. Come back tomorrow.
Another time, then. The offer stands.
Welcome to the Buxton spa, {player}. Water's twenty-eight degrees, all year.
I'm Maud, Keeper of the Brook Stone. I've held it since before the Crescent was a plan.
Brook creatures are patient, you see. They wear down anything. Mountains, even.
Let's see what you and yours can do, shall we? Swimming costumes optional.
Here you are. The Brook Stone. It's smooth, because water is thorough.
Keep it by you. When the old legends wake, a Stone makes them listen.
There are more Stones out there, and more Keepers. Some are less polite than me.
Your phone buzzes. It's Professor Garside, who still calls it 'the wireless'.
{player}! A Stone already? Splendid. I heard from the stones themselves.
Mostly, I heard it from {rival}, who posted it nine times.
A practical note. The Brook Stone teaches your team Hedge-lay, the old craft of parting a bramble without losing a sleeve.
Walk up to a bramble patch and see. Half of the Peak's best footpaths are behind one.
Now the serious bit. The stones at Arbor Low are humming, and the hum is spreading north. Manchester, to be specific.
Go up the Goyt Valley and find a bike shop run by a woman called Bev. She owes me a favour and a kettle.
Pack a flask. And do not feed anything that hums.
The road north from Buxton is open. Manchester is about thirty miles away and, by all reports, wetter.
